analysis:
Both units are head_text excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 3599-4090). The file_changes range map shows the only changed head lines are 3541-3575, a new documentation section on cluster service listeners following the cable and pairing. That range is outside both supplied units, so the change itself was not visible in the head text. The patch excerpt is truncated. The excerpt describes ClusterService.listenerChange rechecking listeners every 5 seconds. It restarts a listener on a changed cable port or address, or on a changed pairing identity, and stops it when no pairing exists. A listener left on an earlier pairing refuses handshakes keyed with a later pairing, which is fail-closed behavior. An unreadable pairing store changes nothing, so a running listener stays up. The pairing identity compares the pins, cluster label, link epoch and edge, and never the edge secret. The control lease listener restarts and stops without a log line, which is a small audit gap, not a regression. Nothing observed weakens pairing authentication.

The visible text in my units (3599-4090) is unchanged context: tensor-parallel share and link probes, sealed all-sum, GLM media, and the prefix SSD tier. The text describes owner-only files under ~/.darkbloom/cluster. It describes a sealed all-sum using AES-256-GCM, with a peer piece that fails to open failing the request. It describes tenant-partitioned prefix scopes, and per-build scoping of served-speed records. Nothing in it is new, and none of it contradicts T-041. This is documentation only and changes no code or controls.

Remaining question: the real behavior of ClusterService.swift and ClusterSetupLinkExchange is not in the supplied evidence. Whether the documented behavior matches the code, and whether restart on a changed cable address opens a window for a stale-pairing or rebinding downgrade, belongs to a pass over the code units. The control-port listener's silent restart and the doc's claim that handshakeRejected covers a later pairing are unverified contracts, not findings.
